summary: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 This bill modifies federal permitting processes to expedite a wide range of projects. It also excludes from federal income tax certain damages from lawsuits relating to sexual acts. The bill limits the scope of the National Environmental Policy Act, including by further limiting the types of federal actions that trigger environmental review, and exempting additional types of projects from environmental review. The bill also limits permit obligations under the Clean Water Act, including by narrowing the scope of review for water quality certifications, extending the term for permits issued under the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System, and limiting the time period for review of permits for discharges of dredged or fill materials. It also shortens timelines for certain requirements concerning threatened or endangered species to expedite permits. Additionally, the bill addresses numerous aspects of energy infrastructure permitting, including by expanding the authority of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to issue construction permits for certain interstate electricity transmission projects; directing FERC to establish ratepayer protections related to certain large computational loads (e.g. data centers); removing permit requirements for onshore oil and gas drilling on nonfederal land; and accelerating renewable energy, geothermal, hydropower, nuclear, or offshore energy projects. It also limits the types of projects that trigger review under the National Historic Preservation Act. Finally, the bill excludes from an individual's federal income tax certain damages received due to sexual acts or contact, regardless of whether there are medical records or observable injuries.
title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
